newsitem.title: UK: Vibrating sunflower wins big prize for UK inventor.
newsitem.headline: Vibrating sunflower wins big prize for UK inventor.

text.p: A young British boffin walked off with more than 2,000 pounds ($3,220) worth of prizes on Thursday when his bright yellow vibrating sunflower won a competition to find the year's most weird but workable invention.

Jonathan Cheifetz remained determinedly reserved about his achievement, saying he had not even entered his "Dynamic Sunflower" for the Mathmos Floogelbinder Challenge and certainly did not want to make too much money from it.

The lanky bespectacled youth seemed to be following in the fine tradition of British inventors, famed for producing remarkable ideas but lacking the commercial nous to prevent them being perfected and produced by foreigners.

Cheifetz fought off most questions with a firm "no comment" but did unwind enough over a glass of champagne to explain the purpose of the vibrating sunflower, which is positioned inside a blue bowl covered with flashing red lights.
"I see it as a substitute for an open fire, which although not very efficient is something which is nice to have. My invention brings a room to life," he told reporters.
The sunflowers, which vibrate more violently the louder the background noise becomes, have been on sale for six months in a London store and sell for around 90 pounds ($145) each.

Other contenders for the prize included The Little Onion Fan, a simple propellor designed to stop the cutters of onions from bursting into tears, and what was billed as the world's first ambidextrous board game.
A mains-powered, infra-red beam-activated, fan-induced cigarette lighter was in the running but a technical hitch prevented the inventor showing its finer points. It failed to light.

The competition was sponsored by Mathmos, a British company which has produced millions of so-called "lava lamps" -- which contain slowly circulating lumps of coloured oils -- since they were invented by former World War Two pilot Craven Walker. ($1=.6211 Pound)
